title: Helm probe defaults for existing probes must keep the previous effective timing
answers: helm upgrade changes probe timing for existing deployments
why is timeoutSeconds set to 1 in the chart values
default probe values for MLflow Helm chart
body:
Convention: default values for probes that already existed must equal the timing the chart previously rendered (or the Kubernetes default where none was set), so `helm upgrade` on an existing release leaves probe behaviour unchanged.
Where: charts/values.yaml probes.liveness and probes.readiness. Values such as timeoutSeconds: 1 and failureThreshold: 3 match the Kubernetes defaults, and initialDelaySeconds 15/5 and periodSeconds 20/10 match the old hardcoded values that were in charts/templates/deployment.yaml.
Why: a reviewer noted that defaulting timeoutSeconds to 10 would raise failure-detection latency for every existing deployment, and the author reverted it to 1 for that reason.
Constraints: applies to probes that already had behaviour. A newly added probe with no prior behaviour (startup, timeoutSeconds: 10) may use a new default. Guidance to raise timeouts for slow health endpoints belongs in charts/README.md "Health probes" as advice, not as a changed default.
applies: Changing defaults in charts/values.yaml for any probe field.
says: Upgrading the deployment release altered container health check timings and failure detection speed.
Keep existing liveness and readiness probe response timings identical across chart version updates.
Why did upgrading our release increase the latency before detecting unhealthy application pods?
Preserve legacy health check interval defaults so upgrades do not disrupt existing clusters.
